title: The tool's own bounded model checker: unit tests of the circuits and the cross-check with JBMC
description: lib/src/bmc is a bounded model checker inside jvmcontract: the generated harness bytecode is executed symbolically over bit-vectors (lib/src/bmc/bits.rs, two's-complement circuits with gate hashing) and a bundled CaDiCaL decides feasibility at every branch and the input of a violation. --engine native uses it alone, --engine auto hands anything outside its fragment (arrays, floating point, static state, JDK calls beyond Math/Integer/Long) to JBMC with a note; the default stays jbmc. This job runs the whole suite in release: the circuit tests compare every operation with Rust's integer semantics on the edge cases; the engine tests prove and refute small harnesses (division by zero as an exception path, loop unwinding, multiplyExact's overflow condition); the integration test the_tools_own_checker_agrees_with_jbmc_on_integer_proofs runs eight property proofs and three regression proofs with both checkers and requires the same verdicts and, where unique, the same shrunk witness, and checks the auto hand-over on an array proof.
expected: exits 0; every test passes, among them bmc::bits::tests::*, bmc::tests::* and the_tools_own_checker_agrees_with_jbmc_on_integer_proofs

resources.notes: the suite took under two minutes in the session with CaDiCaL as JBMC's solver; the bmc unit tests about 30 s
